05 · UI / UX Design

UI/UX design in Puerto Rico for products people use every day

Research, flows, wireframes and interface systems for products that have to be used, not just visited.

Request a quote Call (939) 229-9233

01 · Overview

Our UI/UX design service is for apps, dashboards, customer portals and anything with a login. People do not come to these products to browse. They come to finish a task, and every extra step costs your users time and your business money. We design so that task goes right the first time, through an interface that makes sense without a manual.

We start by understanding the jobs your users are hiring the product to do. From there we shape the information architecture and the flows, and prototype the risky parts early. We test with real people before the engineering bill arrives, because fixing a wireframe costs far less than rewriting code that is already in production.

What you get back is a documented design system your developers can build against without guessing: components, states, usage rules and accessibility included. We work from San Juan with teams in Puerto Rico, the mainland United States, the Caribbean and Europe, in English or Spanish. Fixed scope, fixed price, and everything we deliver is yours.

02 Why it matters

What good user experience design does for your product

01

Fewer errors, fewer support tickets

When flows follow the logic of the people using them, fewer calls ask where things are and fewer forms get abandoned halfway. Your support team handles real problems instead of confusion the interface created.

02

Decisions tested before code

Clickable prototypes and usability testing catch problems while they are still cheap to fix. You reach development with the risky parts already validated, not with a bet that only gets settled in production.

03

A system your developers understand

Every component ships documented with its states, variants and usage rules. Your developers build new screens without inventing patterns, and the product stays consistent even as the team changes around it.

04

Accessible from the first sketch

Contrast, touch targets, keyboard navigation and screen readers are solved in the design, not patched at the end. The product works for more people and meets WCAG guidelines without a round of rework.

03 How we work

How a UI/UX design engagement runs

  1. 01

    Research and journey mapping

    We interview users, review your analytics and talk to your support and sales teams. The result is a journey map showing which tasks matter, where people get stuck today, and what the product needs to solve first.

  2. 02

    Information architecture and flows

    We organise content and features into a structure that makes sense to the people using it. Every key flow is drawn step by step, including error cases, empty states and what happens when something goes wrong.

  3. 03

    Wireframes, prototypes and testing

    Flows become wireframes, then clickable prototypes. We put them in front of real users, watch where they hesitate, and fix it. We iterate until the core tasks get done without help or explanation.

  4. 04

    Design system and handoff

    What was validated becomes the final interface and a documented component library. We stay with your developers through implementation to answer questions and check that what gets built matches what was designed.

05 FAQ

What people ask about this service.

UX is the whole experience: which tasks the user performs, in what order, and where it gets hard. UI is the visual and interactive layer: buttons, type, forms and states. A product needs both. A polished interface on top of a confusing flow still frustrates people, and a good flow behind a clumsy interface still feels difficult. We work on both together, starting with the experience.

It depends on the size of the product, the number of flows and how much research is needed. After a scoping call and a written brief we quote a fixed price, with staged payments tied to sign-offs. The number you approve is the number you pay. If you only need one specific problem solved, such as a design system, a two-week focused sprint may be enough.

It depends on what you need. Many clients already have a development team and hire us for design only; in that case we deliver a documented design system and support the implementation. If the product is web-based and you do not have a team, we can quote the front-end build as part of the same project, with hand-written code, no page builders, and everything owned by you.

Most of our testing is remote. We share a clickable prototype with each participant over a video call, ask them to complete real tasks, and watch where they hesitate or get lost. It works the same with users in Puerto Rico, the United States or Europe, in English or Spanish, and it lets us test with the people who actually use your product.

You receive the user journey map, the information architecture, the flows, clickable prototypes, usability testing findings and a design system with usage documentation. All source files are yours. The point is that your team can keep building on that work without depending on us.
